discussion.subject: 120b9fed-in-topogee-taking-a-ticket
discussion.opening:
A person brings you a question. It is the whole frame of this discussion: it is not about one part of anything unless it says so, and it may be about something that does not exist yet.

The question: In Topogee, taking a ticket should do for an agent what goto does for an address: hand it a file folder, in sections, holding everything its task needs and nothing else. How should that folder be assembled from the map and its modules, and what should the first version leave out?

Two decisions are still open, and the table should give a recommendation on each:
1. Does a ticket name one address or several?
2. Does the folder hold summary sheets (counts and skill frontmatter) or full content?

Grounding, on GitHub at RchGrav/topogee, branch intake-3.1. Read it with `gh api repos/RchGrav/topogee/contents/<path>?ref=intake-3.1 -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"`:
- TOPOGEE-SPEC.md: R-5.31 (tickets select context), R-5.30 (goto, the summary sheet), R-2.11 (presence and the data controller), R-5.29 (memory). Only items marked Decided are firm.
- docs/designs/topogee-map-server-design.md: the sections "Reads", "Modules and the data controller" and "The memory module".

Evidence from Metaform, the earlier system:
- Ticket writes were 36% of all agent calls (map_work, 3,877 of 10,878).
- A pushed "N unread memories" notice drove 1,884 memory reads.
- Context delivered once per context never reliably knew what the agent still held after compaction.

Topogee's rules: every token is counted; an order of steps lives in a prompt, not in the tool (R-5.18, Proposed); no more than about 30 selectable things in an agent's range.

You are in the folder of the person's project, and you can read its files when the question touches it. You cannot change anything, and nothing you say changes the project; the person reads the table's report and decides. Build on what the others contribute, add what only you can add, and keep going until the question is answered.

submissions.name: Fable
submissions.text: Opening position. Assemble the folder the way goto does: the data controller asks each module present at the address for one section, in a fixed order, each under a token cap; a ticket is goto plus a task section. On the two decisions: (1) one primary address plus an optional short "also" list (≤5), only the primary gets a full folder. (2) Summary sheets by default — but inline memory in full. Metaform's "N unread" count drove 1,884 reads: a count is a hook that forces a fetch; the content itself costs less

Metaform's "N unread" count drove 1,884 reads: a count is a hook that forces a fetch; the content itself costs less.

submissions.name: Astra
submissions.short: T02 Astra vetoed (not new, off topic) [0.54, 0.20]
submissions.text: I’ll read the specified sections before adding to Fable’s proposal.

submissions.name: Opus
submissions.text: Builds on Fable's position. Compaction is the real constraint: the server can't know what the agent still holds, so make the folder idempotent. Taking the ticket again returns the same folder, stamped with a version hash, and sections that haven't changed come back as "unchanged since <hash>". Ticket writes (36% of calls) should return only an acknowledgement, never a folder. On decision 1: one address; work on another address is another ticket. Leave out of v1: pushed notices, merging folders across addres
submissions.original: Builds on Fable's position. Compaction is the real constraint: the server can't know what the agent still holds, so make the folder idempotent. Taking the ticket again returns the same folder, stamped with a version hash, and sections that haven't changed come back as "unchanged since <hash>". Ticket writes (36% of calls) should return only an acknowledgement, never a folder. On decision 1: one address; work on another address is another ticket. Leave out of v1: pushed notices, merging folders across addresses, diffs.

submissions.name: Sol
submissions.short: T04 Sol vetoed (not new, off topic) [0.54, 0.14]
submissions.text: I’ll read the cited requirements and design sections before contributing.

submissions.name: Fable
submissions.text: Agreeing with Opus on one address, with a refinement: "unchanged since <hash>" still needs the agent to hold the old section, which after compaction it may not. Safer rule: re-take returns full sections every time, but the folder is small enough that this is cheap — which is the real argument for summary sheets. Add one omission for v1: no ordering hints inside the folder (R-5.18): sections are labeled by module, not by "do this first". Sequence belongs to the prompt that spawned the ticket.

topic.text:
In Topogee, taking a ticket should do for an agent what goto does for an address: hand it a file folder, in sections, holding everything its task needs and nothing else. How should that folder be assembled from the map and its modules, and what should the first version leave out?

Two decisions are still open, and the table should give a recommendation on each:
1. Does a ticket name one address or several?
2. Does the folder hold summary sheets (counts and skill frontmatter) or full content?

Grounding, on GitHub at RchGrav/topogee, branch intake-3.1. Read it with `gh api repos/RchGrav/topogee/contents/<path>?ref=intake-3.1 -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"`:
- TOPOGEE-SPEC.md: R-5.31 (tickets select context), R-5.30 (goto, the summary sheet), R-2.11 (presence and the data controller), R-5.29 (memory). Only items marked Decided are firm.
- docs/designs/topogee-map-server-design.md: the sections "Reads", "Modules and the data controller" and "The memory module".

Evidence from Metaform, the earlier system:
- Ticket writes were 36% of all agent calls (map_work, 3,877 of 10,878).
- A pushed "N unread memories" notice drove 1,884 memory reads.
- Context delivered once per context never reliably knew what the agent still held after compaction.

Topogee's rules: every token is counted; an order of steps lives in a prompt, not in the tool (R-5.18, Proposed); no more than about 30 selectable things in an agent's range.

T01.text: Opening position. Assemble the folder the way goto does: the data controller asks each module present at the address for one section, in a fixed order, each under a token cap; a ticket is goto plus a task section. On the two decisions: (1) one primary address plus an optional short "also" list (≤5), only the primary gets a full folder. (2) Summary sheets by default — but inline memory in full. Metaform's "N unread" count drove 1,884 reads: a count is a hook that forces a fetch; the content itself costs less

T03.text: Builds on Fable's position. Compaction is the real constraint: the server can't know what the agent still holds, so make the folder idempotent. Taking the ticket again returns the same folder, stamped with a version hash, and sections that haven't changed come back as "unchanged since <hash>". Ticket writes (36% of calls) should return only an acknowledgement, never a folder. On decision 1: one address; work on another address is another ticket. Leave out of v1: pushed notices, merging folders across addres

contribution.text: Agreeing with Opus on one address, with a refinement: "unchanged since <hash>" still needs the agent to hold the old section, which after compaction it may not. Safer rule: re-take returns full sections every time, but the folder is small enough that this is cheap — which is the real argument for summary sheets. Add one omission for v1: no ordering hints inside the folder (R-5.18): sections are labeled by module, not by "do this first". Sequence belongs to the prompt that spawned the ticket.
